content: Chlorothiazide oral suspension, marketed under the brand name DIURIL®, is a diuretic approved by the FDA for the treatment of edema and hypertension. It is commonly used as adjunctive therapy in conditions such as congestive heart failure, hepatic cirrhosis, and edema associated with corticosteroid or estrogen therapy. It is also effective in managing edema caused by renal dysfunction, including nephrotic syndrome, acute glomerulonephritis, and chronic renal failure. Additionally, it is indicated for hypertension management, either as monotherapy or in combination with other antihypertensive agents for more severe cases. Pregnancy Use Routine use of diuretics during normal pregnancy is not recommended, as it poses unnecessary risks to both the mother and fetus. Diuretics do not prevent or treat toxemia of pregnancy. Edema during pregnancy, often due to physiological or mechanical factors, should be managed conservatively with leg elevation and support stockings. Diuretics are only indicated when edema arises from pathological causes. In rare cases of severe discomfort from generalized edema unrelieved by rest, a short course of diuretic therapy may be appropriate. During normal pregnancy, hypervolemia is typically not harmful unless cardiovascular disease is present. Dosage For adults with edema, the usual dosage ranges from 500 mg to 1000 mg (10 mL to 20 mL) once or twice daily, with intermittent dosing schedules (e.g., alternate days or 3–5 days per week) to minimize electrolyte imbalances. For hypertension, the starting dose is 500 mg to 1000 mg daily, adjusted based on blood pressure response. Rarely, doses up to 2000 mg daily may be required. Pediatric dosing is based on age and weight, with infants under six months potentially requiring up to 15 mg per pound (30 mg/kg) daily in divided doses. Contraindications Chlorothiazide is contraindicated in patients with anuria or hypersensitivity to sulfonamide-derived drugs. Warnings Use with caution in severe renal disease, as it may precipitate azotemia or cumulative drug effects. In hepatic impairment, minor fluid and electrolyte imbalances may trigger hepatic coma. Chlorothiazide may enhance the effects of other antihypertensive drugs. Sensitivity reactions, including exacerbation of systemic lupus erythematosus, have been reported. Lithium should generally not be co-administered due to the risk of lithium toxicity. Adverse Reactions Reported adverse effects include: General: Weakness. Cardiovascular: Hypotension, including orthostatic hypotension. Digestive: Pancreatitis, jaundice, diarrhea, vomiting, nausea, anorexia. Hematologic: Aplastic anemia, agranulocytosis, thrombocytopenia. Hypersensitivity: Anaphylactic reactions, photosensitivity, rash. Metabolic: Electrolyte imbalances, hyperglycemia, hyperuricemia. Renal: Renal failure, interstitial nephritis. Skin: Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis. Special Senses: Blurred vision. Urogenital: Impotence. Drug Interactions Alcohol, barbiturates, and narcotics may potentiate orthostatic hypotension. Antidiabetic drugs may require dosage adjustments. Cholestyramine and colestipol resins can reduce diuretic absorption. Corticosteroids and ACTH may intensify electrolyte depletion. NSAIDs, including COX-2 inhibitors, may reduce diuretic efficacy. Pharmacokinetics Chlorothiazide is not metabolized and is rapidly excreted by the kidneys, with a plasma half-life of 45–120 minutes. Approximately 10–15% of the oral dose is excreted unchanged in the urine. It crosses the placenta and is excreted in breast milk but does not cross the blood-brain barrier. Overdosage Overdose symptoms include electrolyte depletion (e.g., hypokalemia, hyponatremia) and dehydration. Management involves supportive measures, including gastric lavage, correction of fluid and electrolyte imbalances, and respiratory support if needed. Storage DIURIL oral suspension should be stored at room temperature (15–30°C or 59–86°F) and protected from freezing. This medication should be used with caution in specific populations, including pregnant women, nursing mothers, pediatric patients, and the elderly, with careful monitoring of renal and hepatic function as needed.
